Wastewater contains nutrients, such as nitrates and phosphates, that in excessive amounts may pollute nearby waterways and groundwater supplies. Excessive nutrients in drinking water supplies can be harmful to human health and can degrade lakes and streams by enhancing weed growth and algal blooms. However, the soil can retain many of these nutrients, which are eventu- ally taken up by nearby vegetation.

Solids that are allowed to pass from the septic tank may clog the absorption field. Keeping solids out of the absorption field not only prevents clogging, but also reduces potentially expensive repair or replace- ment costs and helps ensure the ability of the soil to effectively treat the septic tank effluent. Therefore, an additional safeguard in keeping solids out of the absorption field is the use of effluent filters on the outlet of the septic tank (see Figure 2).

GALLAGHER: Well…that’s something I…After talking bout stuff. I said what about the Grove property. That is something that we have…cause they’re looking for ways to actually make this happen. Financially, what kind assets, what kind of contributions. That type of things. And…certainly with any development of that property. And with the firehouse…you’re gonna have to…there’s…you’re gonna have to move things around as much as possible, especially the parking in that area…and how’re you gonna use that building. That’s one that thing we really never addressed. What’s gonna be the use of that building? So that’s something that…it’s really to put that out there as part of this project as a …for sort of brainstorming as how to use that property. Having it being open to a nonprofit or something like that. And to at least think about it in developing a concept on how to use that site, which is just what we’re doing and I would say…you know…as opposed to a change of heart. What happened last week was really the way the process is supposed to be. There’s an idea for how to use this property the county is thinking of buying it. And they go to the municipalities and say how do you want to participate? Which is exactly what he did. That then puts the burden on us then to come back and say hey we gotta come up with some ideas if we wanna make this thing happen. And everybody left that meeting feeling like we’re moving forward and there was sort of a positive energy to to make something happen…and another idea that…was proposed…you know…was or at least thought about was…you know…or if there are ways of combining other services…you know…the highway department of something like that or at least co-locating. I know that the county is certainly looking into probably working more with towns on maintenance of county roads. That type of thing. So, that’s another thing I think that they…to think about. Other ways to…that services or locations could be shared ultimately to save money. Cause this is sorta of like one big giant puzzle. Moving pieces around...of freeing up space here but…you know…moving space there sharing it then you have…you know…a shared courtroom that a little bit higher quality…or shared sheriff…and police department…type of thing. HUSTIS: I also like the possibility with the Grove of reaching out for a nonprofit taking over because you maybe can preserve the historical part of it. Bring some king of historical awareness to the community. I mean…anything good for that building instead of looking at an eyesore right now would be a blessing. GALLAGHER: I hear ya. So on these items…and the seven. We can go…I can go back to County Executive Bondi and Legislator Tamagna and say the village boardss generally in support of these uses.

If you’ve previously used cleaners or chemicals of any kind on the area, then neutralizing cleaners won’t be effective until you’ve rinsed every trace of the old cleaner from the carpet. Even if you haven’t used chemicals recently, any trace of a non-protein-based substance will weaken the effect of the enzymatic cleaner. The cleaner will use up its “energy” on the old cleaners instead of on the protein stains you want removed.
